verdict.summary: You can create a Projects-based OAuth app and connect your own account in under an hour, and an unlisted app can be installed in up to 25 accounts without review. Above 25 accounts you need a Marketplace listing. Listing requires 3 active installs from accounts not affiliated with you, plus a manual review: HubSpot promises a first response within 10 business days, and feedback rounds can stretch to about 60 days.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours to reach a working app; 1-3 days to prepare a Marketplace listing (policy pages, setup docs, scope cleanup)
verdict.approval_wait: none for up to 25 installs; Marketplace listing takes 10 business days for the first review, often 2-4 weeks (reported), up to ~60 days with feedback rounds

gates.name: Developer test accounts (unpublished app)
gates.unlocks: Create the OAuth app and install it in your developer test accounts to run Composio connections yourself.
limits: Until you sign the Acceptable Use Policy, the app installs only in developer test accounts
Access tokens expire after 30 minutes; refresh tokens are used to get new ones
The installing user must be a Super Admin or have Marketplace Access permission

gates.name: Unlisted Marketplace OAuth app (or private distribution)
gates.unlocks: Any HubSpot account can install via your install URL. There is no allowlist, up to the install cap.
limits: Max 25 installs before listing (developer test accounts excluded); applies to apps created on or migrated to platform 2025.2
Private distribution alternative: 10 allowlisted customer portals, or 100 if the app is created in a Solutions Partner portal
Installers see an unverified-app warning/confirmation dialog and must type an explicit risk acceptance
Sensitive-data scopes stay allowlisted for testing only until HubSpot enables them at publishing
gates.time_to_reach: Same day after you sign the AUP; domain verification usually takes under an hour (DNS can take up to 48h)

gates.name: Listed on the HubSpot Marketplace
gates.unlocks: Removes the 25-install cap and the unverified-app warning, so anyone can install.
limits: Requires at least 3 active, unique production installs unaffiliated with you in the past 30 days
Only one app can be in the approval queue at a time
Rate limit of 110 requests per 10 seconds per installing account (the certification page says 100)
Certification is a separate optional tier, available after 6 months listed with 60+ installs
gates.time_to_reach: 10 business days for the first review; up to ~60 days with feedback; 2-4 weeks reported in practice

steps.title: Create a HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: At developers.hubspot.com, choose the option to create a developer account. The pages checked list no paid-plan or partner requirement for this, but confirm it in your own account. Create a developer test account inside it so you have somewhere to test installs.
gotchas: Use a company-owned login. The developer account holds the app, its verified domain and its Marketplace listing.

steps.title: Create a Projects-based app with the HubSpot CLI
steps.detail: Install the HubSpot CLI and create a new project app. When prompted, choose distribution on the HubSpot Marketplace and OAuth as the auth type. A static token limits the app to one account, and any app installed by multiple accounts must use OAuth.
gotchas: A third-party integrator reports that creating legacy public apps has been disabled since mid-2026, so the CLI/Projects path may be the only option.
If you pick private distribution instead, you can switch to Marketplace later, but private apps are limited to 10 allowlisted portals (100 for Solutions Partners).

steps.title: Set the redirect URL in app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: In the app's top-level app-hsmeta.json, add the callback URL from your Composio auth config to the redirectUrls array, then run hs project upload. Production redirects must use https and a domain name, not an IP address.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Copy the exact URL shown in your Composio auth config. Composio's catalog lists one default redirect (.../api/v1/auth-apps/add), but a v3 callback (.../api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback) is also in use, so paste whichever your config shows.

steps.title: Declare a trimmed scope list
steps.detail: In the auth block of app-hsmeta.json, list scopes under requiredScopes, optionalScopes and conditionallyRequiredScopes. Include only what your agent's tools actually call; do not copy Composio's ~40-scope default. The oauth scope is added automatically. Upload the project again.
gotchas: Every required scope must also appear in Composio's scope parameter, or the authorization page shows an error.
Optional scopes are silently dropped when the account lacks the matching tool, so check which scopes were actually granted.
Avoid admin scopes such as settings.users.write or settings.billing.write unless you need them; reviewers will question them.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Open the app in the Projects view, go to the Auth tab, and copy the Client ID and Client secret. Paste them into a Composio HubSpot auth config set to use your own credentials, with the same scopes you declared.
gotchas: Rotating the secret on the Auth tab invalidates the old one immediately. Update Composio at the same moment.

steps.title: Run a test connection in a developer test account
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection and approve it while logged in as a Super Admin of your developer test account. Confirm you get tokens and a working API call. If the install fails, check Monitoring > Logs in the OAuth tab.
gotchas: Access tokens last 30 minutes, and authorization codes are single-use with a short exchange window.
Some scopes also need a matching user permission, for example Import for crm.import.

steps.title: Sign the Acceptable Use Policy
steps.detail: In the app's Distribution tab, click Begin publishing, then review and sign HubSpot's Acceptable Use Policy. Until you do, the app installs only in developer test accounts.

steps.title: Verify your domain
steps.detail: On the developer account's Domain page, add your domain and create the DNS TXT record HubSpot gives you. Verification usually takes under an hour but can take up to 48 hours. Listed apps don't need this, but unlisted apps are expected to have it.
gotchas: A developer account can have only one verified domain, and all its apps share it.

steps.title: Share the install link with up to 25 accounts
steps.detail: Unlisted Marketplace OAuth apps have no allowlist. Anyone with your Composio connect link can install, up to 25 accounts before listing. Tell users they will see an unverified-app warning and must type a risk acceptance to continue.
gotchas: Use a clear app name, description and scope explanations to reduce drop-off at the warning dialog.

steps.title: Request sensitive-data scopes (only if needed)
steps.detail: If you need sensitive-data scopes (for example crm.objects.contacts.sensitive.read), request them from HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team. HubSpot allowlists them for testing first and enables them at publishing after compliance checks. Most of these scopes work only in accounts with an Enterprise subscription.

steps.title: Prepare Marketplace listing assets
steps.detail: Draft and publish live Privacy Policy and Terms of Service pages, a support contact, and public setup documentation (no login or paywall). The docs should cover install steps with a screenshot of the scope approval screen, configuration, usage, disconnecting and uninstalling. Also fill in the install button URL, pricing and Shared data, and allowlist HubSpot's crawler user agent on your site.
gotchas: Don't combine 'HubSpot' or 'Hub' with your app name or logo, and capitalize HubSpot correctly.
Incomplete fields can get the submission rejected or leave the listing in Draft.

steps.title: Meet install minimums and submit the listing
steps.detail: Make sure you have at least 3 active, unique production installs from accounts not affiliated with you in the past 30 days, and that OAuth is the only auth method. Agree to the Technology Partner Program Agreement, then submit the listing for review.
gotchas: Only one app can be in the approval queue at a time. A second submission is automatically rejected.

steps.title: Wait for the Ecosystem Quality review
steps.detail: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team reviews listings by hand and promises a first review within 10 business days. The full feedback cycle should take no more than about 60 days. Third parties report 2-4 weeks in practice. Once listed, the 25-install cap and the unverified warning go away.

scopes.effect: Standard CRM scopes. Declare them as required only if the agent always uses them; otherwise make them optional or conditional.
The installing user also needs the Import account permission.
High-impact admin scope (manages users and permissions) that sits in Composio's default set. Expect reviewer questions about least privilege; drop it unless you need it.
Can change billing settings and paid seats. Likely to draw reviewer scrutiny.

blockers.symptom: New installs fail once 25 accounts have the app
blockers.cause: Unlisted Marketplace OAuth apps on platform 2025.2+ are capped at 25 installs until they are listed.
blockers.fix: Get 3 qualifying installs and submit a Marketplace listing, or use private distribution for up to 10 (or 100 Solutions Partner) portals.

blockers.symptom: Install works only in developer test accounts
blockers.cause: The Acceptable Use Policy has not been signed.
blockers.fix: Go to the Distribution tab, click Begin publishing and sign the AUP.

blockers.symptom: Users see an unverified-app warning and must type a risk acceptance
blockers.cause: The app has not been reviewed and listed by Ecosystem Quality.
blockers.fix: Use a clear name, description and scope explanations, and get the app listed to remove the warning.

blockers.cause: A scope marked required in app-hsmeta.json is missing from the scope parameter Composio sends.
blockers.fix: Make the Composio auth config scopes match requiredScopes exactly, and move rarely used scopes to optional or conditional.

blockers.symptom: A user can't approve the install
blockers.cause: The user isn't a Super Admin and lacks Marketplace Access, or a required scope needs a permission (or super-admin status) the user doesn't have.
blockers.fix: Have a Super Admin install, or make admin-only scopes optional.

blockers.symptom: Listing rejected or stuck in Draft
blockers.cause: Incomplete fields, dead policy or docs URLs (crawler blocked), extra scopes, or naming that uses 'Hub'/'HubSpot'.
blockers.fix: Complete every field, allowlist HubSpot's crawler, trim scopes, and fix naming before resubmitting.

blockers.cause: Only one app can be in the approval queue at a time.
blockers.fix: Wait for the first review to finish before submitting another app.

blockers.cause: Marketplace apps are limited to 110 requests per 10 seconds per installing account (100 per the certification page), and the API limit add-on doesn't raise this.
blockers.fix: Throttle calls per account. Keep errors at or below 5% if you plan to certify.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed HubSpot app for prototyping; it works right away. Register your own app when you want your own branding on the consent screen, control over scopes (Composio's default set is broad and includes settings.users.write), sensitive-data scopes, or your own Marketplace listing. Note that your own unlisted app is capped at 25 installs until it is listed. Put the callback URL from your Composio auth config in redirectUrls, and make Composio's scope list match your requiredScopes exactly.

open_questions: Refresh token lifetime and expiry rules were not confirmed; only the 30-minute access token lifetime is documented in the findings.
PKCE support was not found in the OAuth docs.
It is unconfirmed whether a free developer account can create and publish a Marketplace app with no paid plan or partner agreement.
The logged-in app creation UI was not checked; only the Projects CLI flow is documented.
The May/June 2026 cutoff for creating legacy public apps comes from a third party only.
The burst limit is inconsistent: 110 per 10s on HubSpot's usage page vs 100 per 10s on its certification page.
It is unknown whether Composio's managed HubSpot app is subject to the 25-install unlisted cap.
The full list of scopes that need Ecosystem Quality approval was not found; only the sensitive-data family is confirmed.
It is unclear whether scope approval for Marketplace apps is a separate review from the listing review.
It is unclear whether a verified domain is strictly required before unlisted installs, or only expected (it is a certification requirement and is waived for listed apps).
It is unconfirmed whether test credentials have been replaced by a demo video or walkthrough for listing review (third-party claim only).
